findings.location: accim/sim/preview.py, _energyplus_daily (daily_mean / pmot) and energyplus_running_means docstring; TODO.md entry 'E1: the running mean of ASHRAE 55 ... 0.14 degC above ... 8 January'
findings.problem: energyplus_running_means and compute_setpoints do not reproduce EnergyPlus when the run period starts on 2-30 January (1 <= first <= 29). In ThermalComfort.cc (CalcThermalComfortAdaptiveASH55, v25.1.0) the 'wrapping' branch reads days 1..D-1 of January into DailyAveOutTemp slots 31-D..30 and then the last 30-(D-1) days of December into slots 1..30-(D-1); the scalar avgDryBulbASH is left holding the LAST day read (31 December) and is not reset. At the first BeginDayFlag of the run period the code does DailyAveOutTemp(30) = avgDryBulbASH, overwriting the daily mean of D-1 January with that of 31 December, and that value stays in the 30-day window for 30 simulated days. On 1 January (D=1) and for D >= 31 the last day read is the day before the start, so the overwrite is harmless, which is why the two EnergyPlus tests (1 January and 1 July) pass. The RMOT (CEN 15251) initiation has no such defect (verified in the source: alpha_pow = alpha^(6..0), multiplied by (1-alpha), no division by 1-alpha^7).
findings.evidence: Source excerpt: 'for (i = 1; i <= 30 - calcEndDay; ++i) { avgDryBulbASH = 0.0; ... DailyAveOutTemp(i) = avgDryBulbASH; }' followed later by 'if (BeginDayFlag && useEpwData) { DailyAveOutTemp(30) = avgDryBulbASH; ... runningAverageASH = (sum + avgDryBulbASH)/30.0; shift; avgDryBulbASH = 0.0; }'. Numeric check with Seville_Present.epw, start 08/01: energyplus_running_means PMOT day 1 = 10.7167 degC; EnergyPlus per the source = (sum of slots 1..29 + mean(31 Dec))/30 = 10.5743 degC; difference 0.1424 degC, which equals the '0.14 degC' the implementer observed in a real run from 8 January (TODO.md, found with B5). mean(7 Jan) = 10.18 degC, mean(31 Dec) = 5.91 degC. Starts on 1 Jan and 1 Jul reproduce EnergyPlus exactly (11.4907 and 24.0926 degC, same in both).

findings.problem: T0 of te_ref_nl is the running (max+min)/2 of the hourly values of the day so far (OutT before the first hour ends), so Te,ref drifts within the day (at 01:00 T0 is the night temperature, in the afternoon the day's mid-range). van der Linden et al. (2006) define Ti as the mean of the maximum and minimum of the whole day i, a constant per day. The v03 sketch did suggest the running value, so this follows the proposal, but it is not the source's quantity.
findings.evidence: Lines generated: 'if OutdoorHours > 0' / 'set OutdoorMidRange = (OutdoorMax+OutdoorMin)/2' / 'else' / 'set OutdoorMidRange = OutT' / 'endif' / 'set Tout_metric = (OutdoorMidRange+0.8*Tmid_1+0.4*Tmid_2+0.2*Tmid_3)/2.4'. v03 §11.4: 'Ti = (Tmax,i + Tmin,i)/2'. questions.md 'B1: T0 of te_ref_nl before the first hour of the day has ended' records option (a).
findings.fix: Author decision. Options: (a) keep and document the intra-day variation explicitly in docs 4.2.2 and the CHANGELOG; (b) since the EPW is known, write today's (Tmax+Tmin)/2 as a daily Schedule (Schedule:File or Schedule:Compact generated by accim) read by an EMS sensor 'Schedule Value', so T0 is the day's true mid-range in both backends; (c) lag one day (T0 := Tmid_1, i.e. (Tmid_1 + 0.8 Tmid_2 + 0.4 Tmid_3 + 0.2 Tmid_4)/2.4) when no EPW is given. I recommend (b) with (c) as the no-EPW fallback.

findings.problem: Comfort standard 23 reads Trm from the EnergyPlus CEN 15251 sensor (RMOT). In the steady state RMOT is the alpha=0.8 recursive mean of Aqilah 2025 eq. 7, but on the first day of a run period EnergyPlus uses the 7-term sum (1-a)*(Tod-1 + a*Tod-2 + ... + a^6*Tod-7) WITHOUT dividing by 1-a^7, i.e. about 21 % (0.8^7) below the true running mean, and the deficit decays as 0.8^n. For the typical 1-2 week test periods the comfort temperature of 23 is biased low; the YAML twin 101 (rmot_alpha, Erl initialised from the EPW per D3) does not have this transient, so 23 and 101 give different setpoints for ~3 weeks. In addition RMOT is 0 at the very first timestep of the run period (static setpoint in ComfMod 1, Tc(5 degC) in ComfMod 3 for one timestep). Neither effect is documented in §4.2 (only the B1 section mentions the 1-a^7 difference, for the custom model).

verdicts.summary: The ATHB equations, units and coefficients are exactly those of v03 §11.1 / pythermalcomfort 4.8.1 (verified with inspect.getsource: met_adapted = met - 0.234*trm/58.2, the clo model, ts with met_to_w_m2 = 58.15, the 7 ATHB_PMV coefficients, rounding to 3 decimals); the hook calls pmv_athb rather than re-implementing it; the bisection solves Top with tdb = tr = Top as v03 states, uses the RMOT sensor (CEN 15251 running mean), runs at BEGINTIMESTEPBEFOREPREDICTOR after the ACCIS programs and before the actuators are written, never generates TrendVariable, and the EnergyPlus week (re-run in-process) gives schedule setpoints identical to the bisection (max difference 0.0 K). Setpoint' outputs keep using the ACCIS setpoints, not the ATHB ones that drive the thermostat (undocumented); the range saturation at 10/30 °C is silent; the met of the hook is decoupled from the People activity level; the EnergyPlus test checks the mechanism but not the thermal claim (ATHB_PMV within the band only 77-80 % of the timesteps in the sample model).

The SET setpoints are computed with pythermalcomfort set_tmp (ASHRAE 55 two-node code: limit_inputs=False, round_output=False, calculate_ce=False, position argument) by bisection with tdb = tr = Top, tabulated by RH every 1 % and interpolated; with v, met, clo, position fixed the dependence on RH alone is exact by construction, the interpolation error is <= 0.03 K and the EnergyPlus week (in-process) reproduces the table (0.0 K) and the exact bisection within 0.046 K. Issues: the central justification of the design - 'pythermalcomfort cannot calculate the SET in the callbacks of EnergyPlus' (module/class docstrings, docs 4.9.2, CHANGELOG, TODO) - is an over-generalisation: in this review's environment (Python 3.12.15, numba 0.68.1, pythermalcomfort 4.8.1, EnergyPlus 25.1.0, Windows) set_tmp ran 5196 times inside the BEGINTIMESTEPBEFOREPREDICTOR callbacks of a one-day simulation without any crash, both with a warm-up, without it, and with an empty numba cache (6.2 s JIT compilation inside the first callback). The crash is specific to the implementer's environment (Python 3.14). Consequences: there is no SET output of the zones although the in-callback computation (and EnergyPlus's own Pierce SET output) is available; the hour counters of the ACCIS do not follow the SET setpoints; the thermostat/SET weighting of ta and tr differs (error <= 0.14 K for |tr - ta| <= 3 K).

findings.location: accim/sim/comfort_hooks.py AthbSetpointHook.__call__ / SetSetpointHook.__call__ (write only AHST_Act_<zone>, ACST_Act_<zone>); accim/sim/ems/program_lines.py SET_AST_NO_TOL (l. 599-600), COUNT_HOURS_NO_APP (l. 607), CountHours (l. 230-256); accim/sim/ems/long_term_discomfort.py l. 83-85
findings.problem: The hooks override only the actuated schedules after the ACCIS programs have already run. Everything else the ACCIS reports and counts in the same calling point still uses the adaptive setpoints: ComfHours/ComfHoursNoApp/OccComfHoursNoApp (ACSTnoTol/AHSTnoTol), the C2 long-term discomfort counters, the HoursBelow counters' applicability, and the outputs 'Adaptive Cooling/Heating Setpoint Temperature_<zone>'. In a model with the ATHB or SET hook, the comfort-hour outputs (and Table's comfort hours and Building totals) are therefore computed against setpoints the thermostat does not follow, and the reported 'Adaptive ... Setpoint' columns are not the applied setpoints. Not documented in 4.9.1/4.9.2 or CHANGELOG.
findings.evidence: program_lines.py: 'set ACSTnoTol = ACST-ACSTtol' ... findings.fix: Author decision. Minimum: document it in 4.9.1/4.9.2 and CHANGELOG (comfort hours, long-term indicators and 'Adaptive ... Setpoint' outputs are those of the ACCIS, not of the hook). Better: let the hook count its own hours in Python from the <zone>_OpT sensor and Occ_count_<zone> (new reported globals e.g. ATHB_ComfHours_<zone>, SET_ComfHours_<zone>, with the same ZoneTimeStep convention), and/or write the applied setpoints to new reported globals (ATHB_ACST_<zone>, ATHB_AHST_<zone>) so Table can show them; and make Table skip/flag the ACCIS comfort hours when the ATHB/SET outputs are present.

findings.evidence: Experiments (pecs-eplus: Python 3.12.15, numba 0.68.1, pythermalcomfort 4.8.1, EnergyPlus 25.1.0, Windows x64; sample model with the ACCIS, 15 July, hook calling set_tmp(limit_inputs=False, round_output=False) at every BEGINTIMESTEPBEFOREPREDICTOR via run_simulation(after_programs=[hook])): (1) no warm-up, numba cache populated: success, 5196 calls, first call 0.23 s, later <= 0.047 s; (2) warm-up call before run_energyplus in the same process: success, 5196 calls, first 0.051 s; (3) no warm-up and NUMBA_CACHE_DIR pointing to an empty folder (true JIT compilation inside the first callback): success, first call 6.17 s, later ~1 ms, 5196 calls; EnergyPlus 'Completed Successfully' in all. The docs point to post-processing without giving a helper, and the model prepared by apply_set_setpoints has no Zone Mean Air Temperature / Mean Radiant Temperature outputs, so the post-processing the docs describe is not possible from its CSV (the A6 EnergyPlus test's CSV has only Zone Operative Temperature and RH).

findings.location: accim/sim/comfort_hooks.py SetSetpointHook.operative_temperatures (tdb = tr = Top) vs the operative-temperature thermostat of the ACCIS (0.5/0.5 weighting)
findings.problem: The setpoint is the Top at which SET(Top, Top, ...) = target, while the zone's SET depends on ta and tr with the two-node weights (h_r = 4.7, h_cc ~ 3.0 at 0.1 m/s and 1.1 met, i.e. 0.61/0.39), so holding EnergyPlus's Top (0.5/0.5) at the setpoint does not hold the zone's SET exactly at the target. Also inherent to the table design (ta/tr split cannot be used). Small but undocumented.
findings.evidence: Computed with standard_effective_temperature (RH 50 %, 1.1 met, 0.5 clo, 0.1 m/s): at Top = heating setpoint 21.92 °C, SET = 20.91 (tr - ta = -3 K), 21.02 (0 K), 21.16 (+3 K); at Top = cooling setpoint 27.67 °C, SET = 27.01 / 26.98 / 26.99 -> error <= 0.14 K at the heating and <= 0.03 K at the cooling setpoint. ATHB: ATHB_PMV at Top = cooling setpoint changes by -0.010/+0.012 for tr - ta = +/-3 K.
findings.fix: Document the magnitude in 4.9.2 (and 4.9.1 for ATHB); if method='bisection' is added (previous findings), solve for Top with the zone's current tr - ta offset (ta = Top - d/2, tr = Top + d/2, d from the previous timestep) to remove it.

findings.location: accim/sim/comfort_hooks.py _bisect (below_range/above_range -> the limits of temperature_range), AthbSetpointHook / SetSetpointHook
findings.problem: When the target index is unreachable within temperature_range the setpoint silently becomes 10 or 30 °C (10/40 °C for the SET) with no warning, counter or output; in warm climates/future scenarios with RMOT >= ~33 °C the ATHB cooling setpoint approaches the 30 °C ceiling (29.57 °C at trm = 33, RH 50 %) and saturates beyond.
findings.evidence: operative_temperatures(50, trm): trm=28 -> (21.60, 28.71); trm=30 -> (21.99, 29.02); trm=33 -> (22.62, 29.57). _bisect: 'result = np.where(below_range, temperature_range[0], np.where(above_range, temperature_range[1], ...))' with no record of saturation.
findings.fix: Record saturation (e.g. hook.saturated[zone] counts, or a reported global ATHB_saturated_<zone>) and warn once at the end of the simulation (or in SimulationResult); document it next to temperature_range.

findings.location: tests/core/test_comfort_hooks.py::test_the_athb_setpoints_in_energyplus ('assert pmv.iloc[1:].between(-3, 3).all()') and the absence of v03 test (3)
findings.problem: The EnergyPlus test verifies the mechanism (schedule == bisection of the sensors), not the scientific claim that the ATHB_PMV of the zone is held within [athb_heating_setpoint, athb_cooling_setpoint] in occupied hours with the HVAC on; the only check of the ATHB_PMV output is the trivial range [-3, 3]. The report explains the VRF of the sample model exceeds the cooling setpoint by up to 1 K; this limitation is then left untested instead of being bounded.
findings.evidence: In-process re-run (15-21 July, Seville): ATHB_PMV range -0.237..0.629 (zone 1), -0.240..0.693 (zone 2); fraction of all timesteps within [-0.5, 0.5]: 0.795 / 0.773; cooling setpoints 27.38-28.40 °C, heating 20.35-21.21 °C, RMOT 23.53-26.23 °C. In the SET run, the zone operative temperature exceeded the applied cooling setpoint in 37-39 % of the timesteps, by up to 1.67-1.98 K (all timesteps, occupied or not; provisional diagnostics).
findings.fix: Add a bounded assertion (e.g. ATHB_PMV <= athb_cooling_setpoint + 0.25 in >= 95 % of the occupied timesteps, and the heating side), or use an IdealLoads variant of the sample model for the thermal claim; also assert that the ATHB_PMV output equals athb_pmv(MAT, MRT, RH) of the previous timestep for a sample of rows (the DEVLOG notes only 58 of 1007 rows match within 1e-9 because outputs are timestep means - a check against the sensor values would need the outputs at the start of the timestep or a tolerance).

findings.location: accim/sim/comfort_hooks.py AthbSetpointHook(met=1.1, air_speed=0.1) and apply_athb_setpoints; docs 4.9.1
findings.problem: No unit mix-up was found (the hook, athb_met/athb_clo and pmv_athb all use met; 58.2 W/m² in met_adapted and 58.15 in ts, as pythermalcomfort), but the met and air speed of the hook are independent of the People objects' activity level (W/person) and air velocity schedules that EnergyPlus uses for the internal gains and for its own comfort outputs, so a model can have 1.1 met in the ATHB setpoints and e.g. 120 W/person (~1.15 met with 1.8 m²) in the People. 'air_speed' is passed as pythermalcomfort's vr (relative air speed), while the People air velocity is absolute; the docstring says 'relative air speed' but does not say the user must add 0.3·(met − 1) for met > 1 (pythermalcomfort's v_relative).
findings.evidence: comfort_hooks.py: 'pmv_athb(tdb=..., vr=air_speed, ..., met=met, t_running_mean=...)'; pythermalcomfort pmv_athb source: 'met_adapted = met - 0.234 * t_running_mean / 58.2', 'ts = 0.303 * np.exp(-0.036 * met_adapted * met_to_w_m2) + 0.028' with met_to_w_m2 = 58.15; accim People activity level is W/person (accim.constants.PMV_BODY_SURFACE_AREA).
findings.fix: Document the W/person <-> met relation used by accim (1 met = 58.2 W/m² x 1.8 m² ~ 104.8 W/person) in 4.9.1 and offer met='people' (derive from the activity level schedule of the zone's People objects) as a later option; state explicitly that air_speed is the relative air speed.

findings.problem: (1) Default posture 'standing' for occupants who in the ACCIS use cases are sedentary (1.0-1.2 met); pythermalcomfort's SET uses the radiative factor 0.70 (sitting) vs 0.73 (standing). (2) In pythermalcomfort's two-node code air_speed = max(v, 0.1) and h_cc = max(h_cc, 5.66·(met − 0.85)^0.39) for met > 0.85, so the air speed has no effect below 0.1 m/s and, at 1.2 met, none up to ~0.2 m/s: the user may change air_speed and see identical setpoints.
findings.evidence: Setpoints at RH 50 % (21/27 °C SET, 0.5 clo): met 1.2 with v = 0.1 -> (21.69, 27.67); v = 0.2 -> (21.69, 27.67); met 1.1 with v = 0.1 -> (21.92, 27.67), v = 0.2 -> (22.28, 28.13). pythermalcomfort two_nodes_gagge: 'air_speed = max(v, 0.1)', 'if not calculate_ce and met > 0.85: h_c_met = 5.66 * (met - 0.85) ** 0.39; h_cc = max(h_cc, h_c_met)'.
findings.fix: Author decides the default posture (suggest 'sitting' when met <= 1.2, or require the argument like the others); document the two behaviours of the ASHRAE 55 SET code in 4.9.2 so the insensitivity to low air speeds is not taken for a bug.

findings.problem: (1) The ATHB outputs default to hourly whatever the frequencies of the ACCIS outputs of the model (the tests have to pass ['timestep']); Table then mixes frequencies. (2) met = 0 is accepted (met_adapted negative, ts formula meaningless), while the SET hook warns outside 1-4 met; ISO 7730 uses the PMV for 0.8-4 met (v03 §11.2).
findings.evidence: Signature: output_frequencies: Sequence[str] = ('hourly',); self.met = _check_number('met', met, 0.0).
findings.fix: Default output_frequencies=None -> the frequencies of the model's existing Output:Variable objects of the ACCIS outputs; warn (as SetSetpointHook does) for met outside 0.8-4 met and air_speed > 1 m/s (PMV_INPUT_RANGES).

findings.problem: The three EnergyPlus tests need multiprocessing named pipes; in a restricted environment they fail before running EnergyPlus (not a defect of accim, but it makes the scientific tests unrunnable there and hides the ATHB/SET results).

findings.location: notes/INFORME §2 A4 ('about 1 ms for each zone and timestep'), docs 4.9.1 ('a week of the sample model with two zones takes about 15 s'), DEVLOG A6 ('about 1.5 s: 101 bisections of about 14 ms')

verified_correct: A4 equations against v03 §11.1 and pythermalcomfort 4.8.1 source (inspect.getsource): met_adapted = met − 0.234·trm/58.2; clo_adapted = 10^(−0.17168 − 0.000485·trm + 0.08176·met_ad − 0.00527·trm·met_ad); PMV via _pmv_ppd_optimized(tdb, tr, vr, rh, met_ad, clo_ad, wme=0); ts = 0.303·exp(−0.036·met_ad·58.15) + 0.028; L = PMV/ts; ATHB_PMV coefficients 1.484, 0.0276, −0.9602, −0.0342, 0.0002264, 0.018696, −0.0002909; rounded to 3 decimals; clo=False selects the behavioural adaptation. accim calls pmv_athb (no re-implementation); athb_met/athb_clo reproduce the same formulas (test passes).

A4 bisection: solves tdb = tr = Top as v03 says; ATHB_PMV is monotonic in Top (checked trm 0/15/30, RH 50, 10-30 °C) and the SET in Top (RH 10/50/90, 10-40 °C); tolerance 0.1 K reached in 8 (ATHB) / 9 (SET) iterations < max_iterations 20; out-of-range targets give the range limits; test_the_bisection_brackets_the_setpoints is a genuine bracket test.

A4 sensors/inputs: RMOT (Zone Thermal Comfort CEN 15251 Adaptive Model Running Average Outdoor Air Temperature, α = 0.8 of EnergyPlus) is the running mean; Zone Mean Air Temperature, Zone Mean Radiant Temperature, Zone Air Relative Humidity keyed by the zone of <zone>_OpT; values are those of the previous timestep, 0 at the first timestep of each environment (as the ACCIS).

A4/A6 EMS/API correctness: hooks run at BEGINTIMESTEPBEFOREPREDICTOR only (other calling points return), after the ACCIS programs and before _apply_actuators/_write_reported_variables (controller.py l. 189-196); the objects added are only EnergyManagementSystem:Sensor, GlobalVariable, OutputVariable and Output:Variable - no TrendVariable; without the hook the model with the ATHB objects gives identical results with the EMS and API backends (check_exact=True, re-run in-process) and ATHB outputs are 0.

A4/A6 API: run_ep(hooks=...) with backend='ems' raises NotImplementedError (test passes); hooks are passed as after_programs to run_simulations; hooks are picklable; apply_* refuse mixed mode, models without the ACCIS and a second application; the output IDFs of 1.1.0 models do not change (no EMS code changed; the report's golden master unchanged - not re-run here).

A6: set_tmp is called with limit_inputs=False, round_output=False, calculate_ce=False (correct: calculate_ce disables the met-dependent h_c), position passed; the table has 101 rows (0-100 % every 1 %), np.interp clipped to 0-100 %; with v, met, clo, position fixed and tdb = tr = Top the setpoints depend on RH only (exact by construction); interpolation error <= 0.03 K at half-% humidities; in the EnergyPlus week the schedules equal the interpolated table (0.0 K) and the exact bisection within 0.021/0.046 K.
A6: PPD categories of ISO 7730:2025 Table A.1 mapped to PMV ±0.2/0.5/0.7/1.0 of apply_pmv_setpoints as v03 §11.2 (documented, not new code).
